summary.headline: Jubilant Pharmova Q2 FY27 revenue rose 21% YoY to Rs.2,370 Cr, but PAT fell to Rs.31 Cr as Montreal losses and SPECT shortfall weighed on margins.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to Rs.2,370 Cr across CDMO Sterile Injectables, Allergy, Radiopharma and Generics, with EBITDA at Rs.255 Cr and PAT at Rs.31 Cr. H1 revenue rose 19% to Rs.4,599 Cr, with H1 EBITDA of Rs.523 Cr and PAT of Rs.87 Cr. EBITDA margins declined YoY, driven by the unavailability of high-margin SPECT radiopharma products from Montreal, negligible third-party revenue there, higher opex and remediation costs. Management guided to QoQ margin improvement in H2 with H2 average margins in the mid-teens, and maintained its 2030 net-debt-zero vision.

segments.name: Radiopharma
segments.commentary: Radiopharma margin has declined from about 40% to 32% over the last four quarters as SPECT supply from Montreal is unavailable and lower-margin Ruby-Fill grows in mix. Ruby-Fill grew about 30% annualised in Q2 against a ~35% YoY growth projection.

segments.name: CDMO Sterile Injectables
segments.commentary: Spokane Line 3 generated about $20 Mn revenue in Q2 from 13+ tech transfer projects and 5+ customers. Management reiterated $80-90 Mn peak annual revenue for Line 3, now expected 1.5 to 2 years earlier than McKinsey estimates, with margin pressure during tech transfer.

segments.name: Allergy Immunotherapy
segments.commentary: Strong growth momentum from Q1 continued into Q2; margin improvement expected in H2 from higher production volumes at the Spokane plant.

segments.name: Generics
segments.commentary: Growth continued in Q2 with new launches planned in Q3 and Q4 FY27; company targets 6-8 launches a year and reiterated doubling revenue and 15-17% EBITDA margin over the medium term.

segments.name: API
segments.commentary: API business has been declining since Q3 last year; Q2 decline was about 2%. Pricing pressure continues given the geopolitical scenario; management expects stable run rate unless solvent prices improve.

segments.name: Drug Discovery
segments.commentary: Win rate better than industry and RFP submissions are rising; green shoots expected from Q4 FY27 with ramp-up mainly in FY28. No numeric growth guidance given.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 average EBITDA margin expected in the mid-teens, improving QoQ, supported by SPECT normalisation (particularly Q4), generics launches and higher plant volumes.
Montreal H2 burn to be lower than H1; remediation cost expected to fall by more than low double digits QoQ.
FY27 capex of about Rs.1,800-1,900 Cr; FY28 capex to reduce to about Rs.1,000 Cr.
Net debt zero targeted by end FY2030; FY29 and FY30 expected to be significantly cash-generative.
FY28 guidance to be given in next call; no FY28 margin guidance given yet.
capex_capacity: Ruby-Fill capacity doubling: capex of $67 Mn announced; separate Montreal Ruby-Fill capex of CAD 94.5 Mn (CAD 23.8 Mn government support), capacity online in H2 FY29 with peak ROCE above 20%.
Six new PET sites: cyclotrons deployed at five, one more shortly; first site online in Q3 FY28, two to three sites in that quarter, remaining three in the following two quarters.
Spokane Line 4 build-out complete; media fill qualification done in Q2; tech transfers of one or two projects targeted by Q4 FY27. 23 active Line 4 proposals.
Line 3 at Spokane has 13+ tech transfer programmes; VAI received for Spokane facility; first Line 3 product approved without pre-approval inspection.
Line 4 and PET installation expected complete by end FY27 or early FY28.
demand_pricing: Ruby-Fill growing about 35% YoY; absolute growth this year higher than last year.
Strong US isolator capacity demand cited; management says it can meet it and cites geopolitical uncertainty and industry consolidation as drivers.
Radiopharma margin decline attributed to mix shift towards lower-margin Ruby-Fill as SPECT supply from Montreal is unavailable.
API pricing pressure continues; solvent price easing could improve FY28.
Custom API manufacturing at Nanjangud: one customer served for an off-patent product, with discussions with one more big pharma; no replacement of existing generics volume.

qa_highlights.question: What drives the H2 mid-teens margin recovery?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited new generics launches, SPECT supply stabilising from Montreal (Q4 in particular), and higher H2 production volumes lifting gross margins.

qa_highlights.question: Is Line 3 near peak utilisation at $20 Mn a quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: Management still expects full-year utilisation of $80-90 Mn, with margin improvement as Line 3 moves to commercial production, mainly in FY29.

qa_highlights.question: How much has Montreal cost so far?
qa_highlights.answer: More than Rs.80 Cr lost in Q2; around Rs.157 Cr in H1 and about Rs.200 Cr before that. H2 burn guided to be lower than H1.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 2030 net debt zero vision hold given Debt-to-EBITDA of 2.2x?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes; FY27 is the peak capex year, capex falls from FY28, and new commercial revenue from Line 3, Line 4 and PET is expected to drive cash generation in FY29 and FY30.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected end-FY27 net debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Closer to Rs.4,000 Cr, and management does not expect net debt to rise further in FY28 if plans hold.

qa_highlights.question: Will JBI-802 be commercialised alone or out-licensed?
qa_highlights.answer: Company will complete Phase 1/2 on its own, then consider monetisation options including IPO, venture funding or licensing; data is from 12-17 patients, with ASH presentation in December 2026.

risks_watch: Montreal OAI status and remediation cost trajectory; H2 SPECT supply recovery is key to radiopharma margin recovery to around 40%.
Execution on the mid-teens H2 margin guide, with Q3 and Q4 margin progression and generics launches.
Line 3 tech transfer margins are below commercial levels until FY29; Line 4 could dilute consolidated margins early on.
Radiopharma approval timing: management expects one CRL on a 10-month review, about 13-14 months total for upcoming approvals.
API pricing pressure and geopolitical effects on solvent prices; FY28 API guidance deferred.
MIBG NDA filing planned for Q4 CY2027 or early the following quarter; JBI-802 data at ASH in December 2026.
summary.management_tone: Confident on medium-term growth, Line 3/Line 4 demand and Ruby-Fill, but cautious on near-term margins; management repeatedly declined to give FY28 margin or product-level guidance and deferred several answers to the next call.
key_quotes: we expect margins to improve on a quarter-on-quarter basis with H2 average margins to be in mid-teen.
So, for this quarter, we lost around more than Rs.80 Crores in Montreal.
we are maintaining our vision for 2030.

Spokane Line 4 build-out (media fill qualification done; 1-2 tech transfers targeted by Q4 FY27)

growth.why: Q2 revenue +21% YoY and H1 +19%, with no FY27 revenue growth number guided; H2 margin guided to mid-teens (EBITDA held), capex FY27 Rs.1,800-1,900 Cr and Spokane Line 3 ~$20 Mn/quarter with $80-90 Mn peak, but Montreal losses (>Rs.80 Cr in Q2) and PET/Ruby-Fill capacity mostly land FY28-FY29.

quality.why: Q2 FY27 revenue grew 21% YoY to Rs.2,370 Cr, driven by recurring volume gains in Ruby-Fill (~35% YoY), Allergy momentum and Spokane Line 3 tech-transfer revenue (~$20 Mn in Q2), with no one-off gains or low-base effects cited; the Montreal losses and margin pressure hit profit, not the revenue growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management guided H2 FY27 average EBITDA margin to mid-teens, improving QoQ, from SPECT supply normalisation (Q4), generics launches and higher plant volumes; Radiopharma margin has slid from ~40% to 32% over four quarters and Montreal H2 burn is guided lower than H1 (H1 ~Rs.157 Cr).

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Spokane Line 3 is already commissioned (~$20 Mn in Q2 vs $80-90 Mn peak), Line 4 media fill qualification is done with 1-2 tech transfers targeted by Q4 FY27, and the first of six PET sites is due online in Q3 FY28.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Ruby-Fill is growing about 35% YoY, Line 3 is ramping towards $80-90 Mn peak, and Q2 consolidated revenue rose 21% YoY, though no FY27 revenue growth number was guided and API is declining (~2% in Q2).

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: FY27 capex is firmly set at Rs.1,800-1,900 Cr and FY28 is guided to fall to about Rs.1,000 Cr, with the Ruby-Fill ($67 Mn) and Montreal (CAD 94.5 Mn) programmes already approved, so no fresh major capex is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: No revenue or margin guidance was raised; the FY28 EBITDA guide was deferred to the next call and management was cautious on near-term margins with Montreal still losing money.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 mid-teens margin depends on SPECT supply recovering and Montreal OAI/remediation costs falling by more than low double digits QoQ; any slippage in Q3/Q4 margin progression would be a miss, and Line 3 tech-transfer margins stay below commercial levels until FY29.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Management plans new generics launches in Q3 and Q4 FY27 against a target of 6-8 launches a year, and the MIBG NDA is on track for Q4 CY2027 or early the following quarter.

rows.label: Net debt zero by end FY2030
rows.why: Net debt is expected to be about Rs.4,000 Cr at end FY27 with Debt/EBITDA at 2.2x, capex falls to about Rs.1,000 Cr in FY28, and FY29-FY30 are expected to be significantly cash-generative, though management has not said net debt will stop rising in FY28 with certainty.

rows.label: Montreal OAI status and SPECT supply recovery
rows.why: SPECT normalisation, particularly in Q4, is key to restoring radiopharma margin toward ~40% from 32%, but it depends on Montreal regulatory status and remediation costs, which management has not fixed to a date.

rows.label: Spokane Line 3 reaches peak utilisation
rows.when: FY29 for margins; FY27 for revenue
rows.why: Management still holds to $80-90 Mn full-year peak for Line 3 (about $20 Mn in Q2 from 13+ tech transfers and 5+ customers), now expected 1.5-2 years earlier than McKinsey, but margins stay under pressure until commercial production mainly in FY29.

tone.note: Management was confident on Line 3/Line 4 demand, Ruby-Fill (~35% growth) and the 2030 net-debt-zero goal, but cautious on near-term margins and declined to give FY28 margin or product guidance; analysts pushed on the H2 margin recovery, Montreal cash burn and the leverage path.
